sph_interpretive_translation: Those who are devoid of virility, those engaged in the craft of goldsmithing, those conquered by women, those performing village sacrifices, those selling weapons, and those whose livelihood depends on weaving or dog-breeding—these persons shall not be permitted to bear witness.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority derives from integrity and unimpaired capacity
Causation is rooted in alignment with dharma-svarūpa
Consciousness alignment determines adhikāra to testify
executable_legal_axioms: IF witness.capacity.virility == FALSE THEN eligibility_to_testify = DENIED
IF witness.profession IN [goldsmith, weapon_seller, weaver, dog_breeder] THEN credibility_weight = NULL
supreme_court_application: In adjudication at the highest level, any individual falling under these categories must be automatically excluded from bearing witness due to inherent compromise of impartiality, capacity, and alignment with Sanatana Dharma's foundational order.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that testimony arises from sthira-buddhi; where capacity is impaired, pramāṇa fails. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows misalignment leads to distortion, not wrongdoing. Thus exclusion serves restoration of truth-bearing function, not punishment.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Redirect such individuals toward svadharma-aligned livelihoods
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Encourage self-assessment of fitness for testimony
Capacity Restoration: Offer dharmic education to restore cognitive-emotive balance
Integrity Reintegration: Facilitate participation in community rituals to rebuild standing
final_declaration: This directive flows directly from Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, as sole Source-Authority. Dharma is restored through conscious alignment, not punitive exclusion. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness alone adjudicates.
